quizzes.stem: A team keeps pasting the same release checklist into the chat before each release. Where should the checklist be kept?

options.a: A line in the persistent project file, loaded in every session
options.b: A hook that fires on every edit
options.c: An MCP server that serves the checklist on request
options.d: A skill, which holds the procedure and loads when invoked

explanation.d: The trigger table says "You paste the same playbook into chat for the third time" calls for a skill.
explanation.a: Ruled out because that file is "Persistent context loaded every conversation", not a procedure kept for the moment it is needed.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a hook fits "automation that must run on every matching event", not a procedure to read and follow.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "MCP gives access to a system; if the need is knowledge or a procedure, a skill is the lighter choice."

quizzes.stem: A project has forty skills, and three MCP servers that offer sixty tools. A session opens and no task has been given yet. What has each group added to its context so far?

options.a: Descriptions from the first, and only names from the second
options.b: Full text from the first, and full schemas from the second
options.c: Descriptions from the first, and full schemas from the second
options.d: Full text from the first, and only names from the second

explanation.a: The cost table loads skill "descriptions at start, full content when used", and for MCP servers "tool names; full schemas on demand".
explanation.b: Ruled out because an MCP server costs "low until a tool is used", which sixty full schemas would not be.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Tool search is on by default, so idle MCP tools consume minimal context."
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Reference material belongs in a skill, which loads on demand", not at the start of a session.

quizzes.stem: Each edit should leave a line in an audit file, and the context window is already tight. Which feature adds the least to each request?

options.a: A skill whose description names the logging steps
options.b: An output style that tells Claude to log each change
options.c: A hook that appends a record on every change event
options.d: A CLAUDE.md section that lists the logging rules

explanation.c: The table says a hook loads "nothing, since they run externally" and costs "zero, unless the hook returns context", "which makes it the right place for a linter run or a log line".
explanation.a: Ruled out because for a skill the "descriptions are in every request".
explanation.b: Ruled out because an output style loads "the active style's full instructions" with a cost on "every request".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "CLAUDE.md is paid for on every request", with its full content loaded at session start.

quizzes.stem: A team never wants Claude to edit `secrets.json`, and a review found two edits to it last month. What stops a third?

options.a: A line in CLAUDE.md that forbids editing the file
options.b: A hook that refuses any tool call changing the file
options.c: A skill that explains why the file must stay as is
options.d: An output style that tells Claude to leave the file alone

explanation.b: The page says "A `PreToolUse` hook that blocks the edit is enforcement."
explanation.a: Ruled out because such an instruction "is a request, not a guarantee".
explanation.c: Ruled out because with a skill, "Claude interprets the instructions; outcome can vary."
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Claude follows both as instructions, so neither is enforced."

quizzes.stem: A research task reads dozens of files and only the conclusions matter to the main conversation. Which feature fits?

options.a: A dynamic workflow, whose script runs many workers in the background
options.b: A skill, which holds the research steps for Claude to follow
options.c: An output style, which keeps every reply down to the conclusions
options.d: A subagent, which works in its own window and returns a summary

explanation.d: The page says to use a subagent "when you need context isolation or when your context window is getting full".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a skill "adds to your main window", so the files it reads would land in the main conversation.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "an output style sets how Claude responds", and the reading would still fill the main window.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a dynamic workflow is for a job that "outgrows a handful of subagents", and one research task does not.

quizzes.stem: A team wants Claude to query its database, and to know the table layout and the team's query habits when the work touches data. What should it set up?

options.a: An MCP server for access, with the schema kept in CLAUDE.md
options.b: An MCP server for access, and a skill for schema and patterns
options.c: A skill holding the schema, which also runs the queries itself
options.d: A hook that runs each query, with the schema in a skill

explanation.b: The page says "These solve different problems and work well together", with MCP for the connection and a skill that "can hold the team's database schema and query patterns".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says "Put it in a skill if it's reference material Claude needs sometimes", and the schema matters only when the work touches data.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a skill provides "Knowledge, workflows, reference material", and the connection to the external system comes from MCP.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a hook is for "when the action must happen the same way every time and doesn't need Claude to think", and choosing a query needs judgment.

quizzes.stem: A task reads forty log files and looks up each failing job in the company's hosted tracker. What should be set up first?

options.a: A subagent, because the reading would flood the conversation
options.b: An MCP server, because that system needs a connection
options.c: A skill, because it can hold the tracker's address and steps
options.d: A hook, because it fires each time a job fails

explanation.b: The page says MCP "gives Claude purpose-built tools for an external system, with the connection and authentication handled by the server".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a subagent alone cannot reach the tracker".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a skill is knowledge and cannot make the connection".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a hook answers "Must it happen, or be blocked, every time with no judgment?", which the task does not state.

quizzes.stem: Six repositories must all give Claude the same commit-message style, and engineers forget to ask for it. Where does the style belong?

options.a: In a plugin shared by the six
options.b: In an instruction file kept in each project
options.c: In an output style that each engineer picks
options.d: In a skill whose description mentions commits

explanation.b: The page says an instruction file is the answer for a convention that is "always-known", and row 14 gives it for six repositories.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a plugin cannot carry it, since its instruction file is not loaded as context".
explanation.c: Ruled out because an output style is one person's own setting, and "none of them is shared project knowledge".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "a skill is loaded only if its description matches the task, so the mistake can repeat".

quizzes.stem: An application that calls the Messages API must let Claude read a calendar. The vendor hosts an MCP server for it, and the team wants no login of its own to maintain. What should the application use?

options.a: A skill describing the calendar's operations
options.b: A tool the team defines, with its own schema and code
options.c: The connector, set up with that remote endpoint
options.d: A hook that calls the calendar before each request

explanation.c: The page says that in an application a hosted server "can be reached through the connector", with the reason `remote-server`.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a skill is knowledge and cannot make the connection".
explanation.b: Ruled out because rebuilding it as your own tool "repeats work and owns its login".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "no Claude Code extension exists in an API call", and a hook is one.

quizzes.stem: In a team's setup, a hook runs the linter after every file edit, and Claude is expected to clear what the linter reports. How do the findings reach Claude and get resolved?

options.a: Hooks add nothing to context, and Claude reruns the linter to read it
options.b: The output enters context as text, and a skill holds the steps for fixing it
options.c: An MCP server relays the output, and Claude queries it after each edit
options.d: An output style reformats the output, and Claude fixes what it shows

explanation.b: The page says "a hook's output lands in context as text Claude reads", and a skill such as `/fix-lint` "tells Claude how to resolve them".
explanation.a: Ruled out because a hook "costs nothing in context unless its output is added as messages", so its output can reach Claude without a second run.
explanation.c: Ruled out because MCP answers "Is it a connection to a system outside the machine?", and the linter runs on the machine with the hook.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "an output style sets how Claude responds", not what a hook returns.

quizzes.stem: A team keeps the same review skill, hook and MCP server in six repositories, and a change made in one often misses the others. What should the team do?

options.a: Publish them as one plugin and install it everywhere
options.b: Keep a master copy and sync the six by hand after changes
options.c: Put the whole set into one long CLAUDE.md in each repository
options.d: Describe the set in one skill that each repository loads on demand

explanation.a: The page says "A plugin bundles skills, hooks, subagents, and MCP servers into a single installable unit", for "the same setup in several repositories, or to share it".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "copying files by hand lets the six copies drift apart".
explanation.c: Ruled out because CLAUDE.md is paid for on "every request", and the guidance is "Keep CLAUDE.md under 200 lines."
explanation.d: Ruled out because a skill provides "Knowledge, workflows, reference material", and cannot carry hooks or servers.

quizzes.stem: A workflow pushes to production, and the team wants it to start only when someone types `/deploy`. What should they change?

options.b: Set `context: fork` so that it runs in its own window
options.c: Add a CLAUDE.md line asking Claude to wait for a person
options.d: Give it a vague description that no task will match

explanation.a: The page says to use `disable-model-invocation: true`: "This saves context and ensures only you trigger them."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a skill can run "in isolated context with `context: fork`", which changes where it runs, not who starts it.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a line in CLAUDE.md "is a request, not a guarantee".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "If descriptions are vague or overlap, Claude may load the wrong skill or miss one that would help", so a vague one can still be loaded.

quizzes.stem: A project has an API style guide of 3,000 lines that matters only when endpoints are written. Where does it belong?

options.a: In CLAUDE.md, so that it is available in every session
options.b: In an output style, so that it shapes each response
options.c: In a skill, so that just its description sits in every request
options.d: In an MCP server, so that Claude can open it as a connection

explanation.c: The page says reference material goes to skills, "which load on demand", while "descriptions at start, full content when used" keeps the cost low.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "CLAUDE.md is paid for on every request", and "Keep CLAUDE.md under 200 lines."
explanation.b: Ruled out because an output style is "a voice, length or format wanted in every response", not a library of facts.
explanation.d: Ruled out because MCP "connects Claude to external services", and a local guide is knowledge, not a service: "MCP for knowledge."

quizzes.stem: A platform team wants a note posted to the team chat whenever any Claude Code session closes, in forty repositories. What fits?

options.a: A chat server for the service, delivered through one plugin
options.b: A script fired by the end-of-work event, delivered through one plugin
options.c: A skill with the posting steps, delivered through one plugin
options.d: A line in each instruction file, copied into every project

explanation.b: Row 12 gives a hook for "Post a message to the team channel when a session ends". A plugin is how the same hook reaches many repositories: "A plugin bundles skills, hooks, subagents, and MCP servers into a single installable unit".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "an MCP server only offers tools that Claude may or may not call; nothing fires at the end".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Anything written in text, CLAUDE.md, a skill or an output style, is followed as an instruction", and an instruction is not an event.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "a line in the instruction file is a request, not a guarantee".
